summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, transfusion-dependent anemia likely due to myelodysplastic syndrome, and recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin was admitted for acute worsening dyspnea and orthopnea. She had been intermittently non-adherent with her furosemide and consumed a high-salt diet, contributing to fluid overload. Chest imaging showed pulmonary vascular congestion and a small left pleural effusion. She also reported dysuria, and urinalysis revealed a urinary tract infection; culture grew Klebsiella oxytoca, treated with ceftriaxone. Her chronic left-sided chest pain was deemed musculoskeletal, not cardiac or vascular. She received IV furosemide with clinical improvement and was transitioned to oral torsemide. Her hemoglobin remained stable, and she was discharged home on improved symptoms with follow-up plans for INR monitoring, heart failure management, and repeat chest imaging.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Klebsiella pneumoniae [K. pneumoniae] as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
